title: Email HTML injection
summary:
### Summary When an admin enables custom email templates, Immich substitutes user-controlled values (display names, album names, usernames) into the template via raw string replacement with no HTML escaping, and then renders the result via React's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Any normal user can plant arbitrary HTML - phishing links, image tags, attribute-rewriting payloads, sometimes script - into the emails the admin-configured templates send to other users. The default templates aren't affected; the bug only triggers when custom templates are configured, but the injected content comes from ordinary users with no special privileges. ### Details The substitution function does not escape its inputs - `server/src/utils/replace-template-tags.ts:1-5`: ```ts export const replaceTemplateTags = (template: string, variables: Record) => { return template.replaceAll(/{(.*?)}/g, (_, key) => { return variables[key] || `{${key}}`; }); }; ``` The resulting string is then dropped into the React tree as raw HTML - three email components are affected: **`server/src/emails/welcome.email.tsx:44`:** ```tsx {customTemplate && (
)} ``` **`server/src/emails/album-invite.email.tsx:43`** - same pattern. **`server/src/emails/album-update.email.tsx:42`** - same pattern. The tag values fed into the substitution are all user-controlled: | Template tag | Source | Who controls it | |--------------|--------|-----------------| | `{senderName}` | The sharing user's `name` field | Any user | | `{recipientName}` | The recipient user's `name` field | Any user | | `{displayName}`, `{username}` | User registration | Any user | | `{albumName}` | Album creator | Any user | | `{password}` | Admin-set when creating accounts | Admin (less interesting) | Custom templates are an admin-only opt-in setting, which is why this is Medium rather than High - but the bug is exploitable by ordinary users once an admin turns the feature on. ### PoC **Configuration:** an Immich instance running v2.7.5 where the admin has enabled a custom album-invite template. The template must contain at least one user-controlled placeholder like `{senderName}` or `{albumName}`. **Reproduction steps:** 1. **As an attacker** (any normal Immich user), update your display name to a phishing payload: ``` PATCH /api/users/me { "name": "

Reset your password

" } ``` 2. Or, equivalently, create an album whose name is the payload: ``` POST /api/albums { "albumName": "" } ``` 3. Share that album with the victim. 4. The server renders the configured custom template, substitutes your display name / album name with no escaping, and emits the resulting HTML inside `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. 5. The victim receives an email that, depending on their mail client, renders: - **Always:** a phishing link styled as legitimate Immich content, on the legitimate domain. - **Some clients (legacy webmail, certain mobile clients):** active JavaScript in the mail-origin context. **Source-level reproduction (vitest):** A complete vitest PoC for all five findings in this audit is published as a secret gist: Download into the Immich server workspace and run: ```bash curl -sL https://gist.githubusercontent.com/Dredsen/b423a6c62cdb561b712803643a21b8fb/raw/security-pocs.spec.ts \ -o server/src/services/security-pocs.spec.ts cd server pnpm install pnpm test src/services/security-pocs.spec.ts --run ``` Test relevant to this finding: - `Finding 3: email template HTML injection > replaceTemplateTags does NOT html-escape attacker-controlled values` The key as...
